name: AWS EC2 P4d / P4de (NVIDIA A100 SXM4 40GB and 80GB)
region: us-east-1, us-west-2 on-demand; Capacity Blocks in us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-2 only
price_basis: per A100 GPU-hour. p4de.24xlarge = 8x A100 80GB, on-demand $27.44705/instance-hr / 8 = $3.4309 (us-east-1 and us-west-2 identical). p4d.24xlarge = 8x A100 40GB, on-demand $21.95764/8 = $2.7447, Capacity Block $11.8/8 = $1.475; p4de Capacity Block $17.712/8 = $2.214. Fetched 2026-10-03. PRICE CLASS: this is a PUBLISHED LIST PRICE - an asking rate a new customer is quoted, not a realised, discounted or negotiated transaction rate. A real bill is at or below this and typically well below it once commitments, credits and committed-use discounts are applied.
notes:
A100 remains the value entry point into AWS for anyone who does not need Hopper. p4d carries the $0.00 sentinel too, so treat on-demand p4d as allocation-only and buy the Capacity Block. The 2026-10-07 forward schedule LOWERS P4d Capacity Blocks to $1.696 per A100-hour and P4de to $2.546 - the one AWS accelerated SKU in this slice that is scheduled to get cheaper. P4 Capacity Blocks are offered in only three regions (n. Virginia, Ohio, Oregon), less regional choice than P5. Prices exclude the OS fee ($0 on Linux, $1.0368/instance-hr for RHEL on a 24xlarge) and all data egress. Note p4de is the 80GB part and p4d the 40GB part - different accelerators, not two sizes of one instance, so do not average them.

 EXPORT CONTROL (2026-10-04, mechanism-level; sources spl-bis-2026-05-d5-guidance, spl-bis-2026-01-advanced-computing-case-by-case): renting capacity does NOT remove the export-control question, it relocates it. Providing remote access to controlled computing capability can constitute a transfer under the EAR, so the provider must screen the end user; and separately, under the 91 FR 1684 licence regime the consignee must run KYC procedures to prevent unauthorized remote access and must manage and limit IaaS access to the hardware - obligations pushed onto the customer, who must be told to implement them. For a customer headquartered or parented in Country Group D:5 or Macau the 742.6(a)(6)(iii)(A) end-user/parent test can bite even when the capacity is consumed in a permitted region. Recorded true because the underlying hardware is controlled and the provider carries the screening duty, not because access to a US region is itself restricted.

 LEAD TIME: null, correctly so, and this instance family is the clearest case in the slice. p4d/p4de are the older A100-generation shapes and are listed on-demand, so capacity is allocated per request and there is no wait to quote - the binding constraint for these shapes is instance AVAILABILITY in the region, not a build or ship interval. Recorded on this record rather than invented. The one AWS family that does publish a commitment horizon is Capacity Blocks, whose 8-week MAXIMUM booking horizon is documented (source spl-aws-capacity-block-booking-horizon) and is recorded on rent-aws-ec2-gpu-hourly-2026-10-04, where the Capacity Block prices already live; that 8 weeks is a ceiling on how far ahead you may commit scarce capacity, not a delivery time, and it does not apply to the on-demand rates on this record. Probe log in source spl-negative-no-oem-publishes-lead-time.
